column1: # boru Language Specification: scalar edge cases 3 — strings, atoms, booleans
# String-edge coverage via boru:string-util (the empty string through
# every word, byte-vs-rune semantics on multi-byte text, replace's
# interpolation), the EmptyString/ProperString membership split, Atom
# distinctness, boolean truthiness coercion and connective strictness,
# and the scalar↔String conversion words with their malformed-input
# errors. Complements string.tsv, module-string.tsv and boolean.tsv.
# §1  the empty string through every string word

column3: upper of empty is empty
lower of empty is empty
trim of empty is empty
splitting the EMPTY string yields the empty list, not ['']
…even with the empty separator
the empty needle is contained in everything
…including the empty haystack
a real needle is never in the empty haystack
the empty needle matches at position 0
…also in the empty haystack
haystack-last: nothing is found IN the empty string
replace in the empty subject is a no-op
an empty search string inserts once at the front (first-occurrence default)
repeat 0 is the empty string
repeating the empty string stays empty
padding the empty string is all spaces
changecase of empty is empty
normalize of empty is empty

column1: # §2  ONE character unit — every string count and index is CHARACTERS
#     (Unicode runes), matching the occurrence ops mul/pow (NUR007 fix —
#     this section previously pinned size/indexof/pad as BYTE-based
#     while split/mul/pow walked runes, and slice could cut a rune in
#     half into invalid UTF-8). Byte-level work is the Bytes type.

column3: size is the CHARACTER length: é is one character
three CJK characters
…the byte length lives on Bytes: é is two bytes in UTF-8
split '' walks the same five characters size counts
multi-byte runes split cleanly, never mid-byte
indexof reports a CHARACTER index (h=0 é=1 l=2)
…and {from} is a character index too (the second l)
slice cuts at character boundaries
…never through a multi-byte rune (was invalid UTF-8)
a negative start drops characters from the end
a negative end counts back from the end, in characters
an over-length end clamps to the character length
a start past the end is the empty string
an inverted range is the empty string
a negative start past the front empties
…and so does a negative end past the front
{occ: last} reports the last l's character index
a {from} past the character length finds nothing
…and a {from} AT the character length searches the empty tail
replace clamps an over-length {from} — nothing to the right, unchanged
case-insensitive indices are character indices too
a multi-byte SEPARATOR works
replace is rune-safe
repeat is rune-faithful on multi-byte input
pad pads to a CHARACTER width: ñ + 3 spaces
match indices are character indices too
an empty pattern matches at every character BOUNDARY, end included (PR #306 review)
…and the default first-scope reports the leading boundary
insensitive shell offsets stay in the ORIGINAL string (İ narrows when folded — PR #306 review)
a multi-byte fill pads whole characters
the byte cap holds under a multi-byte fill — checked as a PROJECTION, before allocating (PR #306 review)
ß has no simple-case uppercase — it survives (no SS expansion)
simple case mapping: no final-sigma ς at the word end
accented Latin uppercases per rune

column1: # §3  split / concat round-trips and separator edges

column3: split '' then concat is the identity
split on a separator then concat DROPS the separators
split DROPS empty fields: adjacent separators leave no trace
a lone separator splits to NOTHING (both fields empty, both dropped)
a trailing separator adds no empty field
{scope:'all'} replaces every occurrence
{count} WITHOUT {scope:'all'} is inert — still first-only
{scope:'all' count:2} caps at two — here that is all of them
{scope:'all' count:1} caps at one
matches are non-overlapping, left to right
empty search with {scope:'all'} inserts at every boundary
no match is a no-op, not an error

an Atom interpolates as its bare name
a BigInteger keeps its 0d prefix
template literals nest inside ${} holes

a type literal interpolates as its name

column1: # §6  EmptyString / ProperString — '' is a String but NOT a ProperString

column3: the empty string has its own leaf
non-empty strings are ProperString
both leaves sit under String
…but '' is excluded from ProperString
and 'x' from EmptyString
concat of empties stays empty
…and stays on the EmptyString leaf
one proper operand makes the result proper
a ProperString param REJECTS the empty string
…and accepts any non-empty one
an EmptyString param accepts only ''
…and rejects everything else
a String param spans both leaves

column1: # §7  atoms — quoted words are data, distinct from equal-looking strings

column3: /q quotes a word into an Atom
an Atom never equals the same-spelling String
Atom equality is by name
different names differ
Atoms order lexically among themselves
cross-family ordering vs a String is rejected (use tcmp)
tcmp still orders them: the Atom band sits below Strings
an Atom key reads the same slot as the string key
…and an Atom-keyed set writes the same slot
Atom → String surrenders the name
String → Atom mints an Atom
…equal to the directly-quoted one
Atoms sort lexically
Atoms are truthy
…under not as well

column3: Integer 0 is falsy
Float 0.0 is falsy
-0.0 is falsy too (it equals zero)
the empty string is falsy
none is falsy
an EMPTY map is falsy
a non-empty string is truthy
a non-zero number is truthy
NaN is TRUTHY — only exact zero is falsy
not applies the same coercion
…including NaN-is-truthy
empty string
none

column1: # §9  connectives — value semantics, strict operands, coercing xor

column3: a paren operand evaluates BEFORE and sees it: no short-circuit rescue
or returns the right operand when the left is falsy…
…even when the right is falsy too (the LAST falsy wins)
or of none picks the right operand
otherwise falls through ONLY for none — 0 passes
…and false passes too
guard is STRICTLY Boolean — no truthiness coercion (contrast if)
xor COERCES truthiness (returns a Boolean, unlike and/or)
two falsy strings xor to false
none is falsy, 1 is truthy
the derived connectives coerce truthiness too
implies on falsy operands (false → false is true)
all of nothing is vacuously true
any of nothing is false
all coerces element truthiness
any over all-falsy elements
a none element fails all
and returns the deciding operand — here the falsy none
…from either side

column1: # §10  scalar ↔ String conversion — round-trips and malformed inputs

column3: signed decimal parses
a leading + is accepted
a bare leading dot parses
underscore separators are allowed in Float strings
the special literals parse from strings
…including the negative infinity
scientific notation parses to a Float
Boolean is coercion by presence — content is not parsed
the empty string is the only false String
the text 'false' is not parsed — a non-empty String is true
ANY non-empty text is true — even 'no'
numeric zero converts to false
non-zero Float converts to true
arbitrary-precision zero converts to false, like every other numeric zero
…and a non-zero BigInteger is true — the Big leaves are NOT uniformly falsy (was: every Big value false)
…nor is a non-zero BigDecimal
…while a BigDecimal zero is false
the same rule reaches `if`: a non-zero Big value takes the true branch
…and a Big zero takes the false branch
…and `make Boolean`, the third consumer of the one truthiness rule
truthy option: a YAML boolean token parses
…and 'no' parses to false
…YAML tokens are matched case-insensitively
…surrounding whitespace is trimmed
a non-token string falls back to presence coercion (non-empty → true)
…and the empty string falls back to false
truthy leaves a non-String source to ordinary coercion
truthy:false is plain presence coercion — 'false' is non-empty → true
NUR053: the SOURCE domain is Any — a non-empty List coerces, as `if` and `make Boolean` always did
…and an empty List is false
…a non-empty Map is true
…an empty Map is false
…and none is false: the three falsy members that used to raise signature_error
…and `make Boolean` agrees exactly: the two CONSTRUCTORS now share a domain, not just a rule (NUR053)
`if` agrees for every shape it reads as a VALUE — an empty Map is false
…and a non-empty Map is true
…and none is false, matching both constructors
but a LIST condition is CODE, not a value: `if` RUNS it (the body yields 0, which is falsy) — NUR070
…while both constructors coerce the same list by presence: non-empty → true. `if` and the constructors give OPPOSITE answers here (NUR070)
…and `make Boolean` agrees with `convert`, not with `if`
the options form takes the wider domain too — truthy's YAML parse falls back to presence
…and falls back for none as well
an option explicitly set to none means "not supplied" — the pattern's `tor None` arm, so presence coercion applies

a typo'd option key is a LOUD error. With an `Any` source a PATTERN here would be a trap: the map would fail the pattern, fall back to the 2-arg row, and be coerced AS THE SOURCE — answering true while 'no' stranded on the stack (NUR053)
…and a wrong-typed option value is caught the same way, by the handler rather than by a pattern
the SCALAR options form is untouched — it keeps its pattern, since its source slot is Scalar and cannot swallow a map
NUR053 widened the BOOLEAN target only: an Integer target has no total presence rule, so a List source still has no signature
…and a String target likewise stays Scalar-sourced
…none is declined for a non-Boolean target for the same reason
truthy is inert for a non-Boolean target
Float → Integer truncates toward zero
…for negatives too
Float → String
Boolean → String
specials stringify to their parseable literals
int64 max stringifies exactly
String → Integer → String round-trip
Integer → String → Integer round-trip
